claims.text: NbTiAlZr is a refractory high-entropy alloy system suitable for the proposed high-temperature study.
Aging at approximately 950°C for 1–2 hours followed by controlled cooling will induce a uniform dispersion of fine, coherent L12 nanoprecipitates in NbTiAlZr.
The L12 nanoprecipitates will reside within a ductile matrix.
Minor alloying additions or thermal-profile modifications can stabilize the nanoprecipitates against coarsening.
The nanoprecipitates will impede dislocation motion through the Orowan bypass mechanism.
Retarding precipitate coarsening at service temperature will maintain the strengthening effect.
The aged alloy will exhibit an approximately 20–30% increase in high-temperature yield strength relative to the fully solutionized baseline.
The predicted strength improvement will hold at approximately 1000°C under quasi-static tensile or dynamic compressive loading.
Room-temperature ductility will be retained after aging and minor alloying modifications.
Room-temperature mechanical performance will remain comparable to that of the untreated alloy.
The as-cast initial NbTiAlZr alloy is homogeneous and has a solid-solution microstructure.
The relevant baseline is a solutionized, unaged NbTiAlZr alloy.
Precipitate coarsening during prolonged high-temperature exposure could compromise the strengthening effect.
Deviation from optimized aging parameters could reduce strengthening or impair ductility.
Minor alloying adjustments may form brittle phases if not precisely tuned.

contradictions.description: The initial material is described as as-cast, whereas the baseline is described as solutionized and also as the initial state; these are distinct processing states.

The intervention is presented as an aging treatment but also includes unspecified compositional changes. Comparing an aged, compositionally modified batch with an unaged baseline would not isolate aging as the single intervention.
